title: Kikwiflow Process Definition (.kikwi)
description: Schema for ProcessDefinitionDeployRequest — the JSON payload deployed via POST /process-definitions to the Kikwiflow engine (see kikwi-model's io.kikwiflow.model.definition.process.ProcessDefinitionDeployRequest and each FlowNodeDefinition subtype). Source of truth for every field/rule here: kikwi-model (plain Java records, no Bean Validation annotations — nothing is truly 'required' at the model level) and kikwi-core's DeployValidator (the only place that actually rejects a deploy). Verified against commit b21da09 (2026-08-21) plus the uncommitted addition of SequenceFlowDefinition.extensionProperties/labelPosition/sourceHandle on the same date (added to support the kikwi-pulse-ui edge-label/edge-documentation feature), and the ~50 fixtures under kikwi-core-tests/src/test/resources/processes. If the engine evolves, re-check field lists against those two locations before trusting this file over the source.
$comment: Deliberately excluded (confirmed by grep — zero hits in any .java file as of the commit above): variableDeclarations / preConditions / postConditions / postConditionsProviderBean (docs/engine/26 — an unimplemented spec), candidateRoles / role-based task authorization (docs/engine/24 Part B — unimplemented), FormDefinition/FormComponentDefinition (exists in kikwi-model but orphaned — never referenced by any FlowNodeDefinition), transitionType on sequence flows (appears in some prose docs and in the document-java-as-kikwi skill's examples, but SequenceFlowDefinition has no such field). Two validation tiers are used throughout this schema: tier A = actually enforced today by DeployValidator, modeled here as real if/then/required constraints; tier B = documented behavior/expectation that the engine does NOT enforce at deploy time (e.g. defaultStartPoint or targetNodeId resolving to a real node) — these are described in prose only and never turned into a required/enum constraint, so this schema never rejects a process the engine would accept.

key.description: Process definition business key — the identifier used by KikwiflowEngine.startProcess().byKey(...).

sla.description: Present on the model but unused anywhere in kikwi-core today (grep for .sla()/getSla in kikwi-core returns zero hits) — vestigial, accepted by the parser but has no functional effect.

defaultStartPoint.description: Should be a key present in flowNodes, identifying a DEFAULT_START_EVENT node. NOT validated at deploy time (tier B) — KikwiflowEngine only resolves it the first time a process instance is started, and throws a null-derived error then if it doesn't resolve.

flowNodes.description: Keyed by node id — each value is a polymorphic FlowNodeDefinition dispatched by its own "type" field. By convention the map key should equal the node's own "id" field, but that consistency is never checked by the engine.

extensionProperties.description: Free-form string-to-string bag (Map<String,String> in the model) — untyped/unused by the engine core itself, available to downstream consumers (UI, custom extensions). Two reserved keys are used by convention (kikwiflow-pulse-ui, the visual modeler): 'kikwi:documentation' (free-form Markdown, may include ```mermaid fenced blocks) and 'kikwi:documentationLink' (a URL, opened in a new tab, or a path relative to the project, which only resolves inside the VS Code extension) — by UI convention the two are mutually exclusive (embedded doc vs. link), but the engine treats extensionProperties as an opaque bag and enforces nothing about these keys; this schema doesn't either. Present at process, node and (as of this addition) sequence-flow level.

layoutCoordinates.description: Diagram positioning only — has no effect on execution.

sequenceFlow.description: Lives inside a node's own "outgoing" array — there is no separate top-level sequence-flow collection; every node owns its own outgoing edges.

expectedAnswer.description: Only meaningful on EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY outgoing edges — the Navigator compares this by plain string equality against whatever the gateway's AnswerProvider resolves to. There is no expression/condition language in Kikwiflow, just string matching.

targetNodeId.description: Should be a key present in the process' flowNodes map. NOT validated at deploy time (tier B) — an unresolved id only fails the first time this edge is actually taken, at runtime.

isDefault.description: At most one outgoing edge per EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY may set this true — DeployValidator rejects a gateway with more than one default edge (tier A, enforced separately on the owning EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY.outgoing array by this schema). Taken when the resolved answer is non-null and no expectedAnswer matched.

handlesNull.description: Taken when the gateway's AnswerProvider resolves to null — checked ahead of expectedAnswer/isDefault matching.

positionHandlers.description: Intermediate waypoints for diagram rendering only — no effect on execution.

extensionProperties.description: A real, persisted field on SequenceFlowDefinition (added to support kikwi-pulse-ui's edge documentation feature — see the reserved-keys note on the shared extensionProperties definition). Unlike the node/process-level extensionProperties (still nullable), this one is normalized at the model level: omitted or null input is turned into {} by SequenceFlowDefinition's compact constructor and never surfaces as null once deployed.

labelPosition.description: Only set when the user manually drags the edge's label chip in the visual modeler (kikwi-pulse-ui's GatewayFlowEdge, mainly relevant on EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edges). Absent/null means the UI recalculates the label position automatically on every render — do not synthesize a default {x,y} here or downstream; round-trip exactly what was saved.

sourceHandle.description: Opaque identifier of the source node's outgoing visual handle in the modeler's React Flow graph (e.g. "right", "right-2", "right-3" when a node has more than one visual output on the same side). The engine has no closed vocabulary of valid handles — this is UI-defined and passed through as plain text, purely for re-rendering the diagram the way it was last edited.

id.description: Should equal this node's own key in the process' flowNodes map — the engine resolves cross-references (targetNodeId, attachedToRef, boundaryEventIds, ...) against that map key, not against this field; a mismatch between the two is never checked.

commitBefore.description: When true, the Navigator persists a UnitOfWork and returns control immediately instead of continuing synchronously — Kikwiflow's actual async-continuation mechanism. This is unrelated to BPMN asyncBefore XML; there is no message bus, a separate TaskAcquirer/TaskExecutor later polls for the pending work.

outgoing.description: null when omitted from the JSON — Jackson does not apply an empty-array default on this record field, so an omitted "outgoing" and an explicit "outgoing": null mean the same thing at runtime, NOT [].

retryPolicy.description: Only used by EXECUTABLE_TASK.retryPolicy. When null entirely, the engine falls back to the app-level kikwiflow default-retry-interval config instead of any of these fields.

initialInterval.description: ISO-8601 duration (e.g. "PT10S"). Semantically required as the base interval when strategy is EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF — not enforced at deploy time (tier B).

multiplier.description: EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF only. Defaults to 2.0 at runtime when null.

maxInterval.description: ISO-8601 duration cap on the computed interval. EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF only.

intervals.description: LINEAR only — ISO-8601 durations indexed by attempt number, clamped to the last entry once the list is exhausted. Falls back to a hardcoded PT1M if empty/null.

type.description: CRON was deliberately removed from this enum (never fully implemented — it was silently treated as an ISO-8601 duration, not real cron syntax — and making it real would require a vendor-specific SPI, which conflicts with the engine's vendor-neutral design). Do not expect a CRON value here even in future engine versions unless that design decision is revisited.

fixedDates.description: FIXED_DATES only — ISO-8601 instants (e.g. "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"); the evaluator picks the first future date in this list.

maxOccurrences.description: 1-based cap on recurrence cycles — with maxOccurrences=3 the timer fires on cycles 1, 2 and 3 and never schedules a 4th. null means unbounded recurrence (legacy behavior).

value.description: Literal text when type=LITERAL, or the name of a process variable to interpolate when type=VARIABLE.

correlationTemplate.description: One entry expected per key when the owning node's catchType=GROUP; a single entry for STANDALONE.

correlationKeySourceBase.description: Shared correlation-key resolution contract (CorrelationKeySource) — implemented by EVENT_CATCHER, BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_CATCH_EVENT and EVENT_THROWER. All four providerType-conditional requirements below ARE enforced at deploy time by DeployValidator.validateCorrelationKeySource (tier A), identically for all three node types.

providerBean.description: CorrelationKeysProvider Spring bean name — required non-blank and resolved at deploy time when providerType=BEAN.

providerVariable.description: Process variable name — required non-blank at deploy time when providerType=VARIABLE.

staticKey.description: Literal correlation key — required non-blank at deploy time when providerType=STATIC.

correlationTemplates.description: Required non-empty at deploy time when providerType=TEMPLATE.

flowNodeUnion.description: One entry of the process' flowNodes map. Dispatched on "type" — each branch below routes to the matching $defs/nodeTypes/* schema, which independently closes itself against unknown fields (typos surface as "unevaluated properties" there, scoped to the matched node type).

type.description: Discriminator — must exactly match one of the 15 @JsonSubTypes values FlowNodeDefinitionMixin dispatches on.

startEvent.description: DEFAULT_START_EVENT — no node-specific fields beyond the common base.

endEvent.description: DEFAULT_END_EVENT — no node-specific fields beyond the common base.

executableTask.description: EXECUTABLE_TASK — runs a Java TaskHandler synchronously on the acquiring thread.

executor.description: Spring TaskHandler bean name. Resolved and validated at deploy time only when non-blank (tier A) — a blank/omitted executor deploys fine and only fails the first time this node is actually reached.

boundaryEventIds.description: Ids of boundary events attached to this task. Deploy-time allowlist (tier A, but the referenced ids' own types are NOT checkable by this schema — cross-node reference): only BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER or BOUNDARY_ERROR_HANDLER. Interruptive timers/catch events are forbidden here — this task runs its handler synchronously with real side effects and has no safe interruption point mid-execution.

externalTask.description: EXTERNAL_TASK — a wait state, completed from outside the engine (a worker calling the REST/client API).

boundaryEventIds.description: Ids of boundary events attached to this task. No dedicated allowlist branch exists in DeployValidator for this host type — each boundary event enforces its own rule instead (e.g. BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_CATCH_EVENT independently requires its attachedToRef to resolve to an EXTERNAL_TASK or TIMER_TASK).

exclusiveGateway.description: EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY — routes to exactly one outgoing edge, chosen by string-matching an AnswerProvider's resolved answer against each edge's expectedAnswer.

defaultFlow.description: Informational only — the Navigator never reads this field at runtime; only outgoing[].isDefault decides the actual default edge.

providerBean.description: AnswerProvider Spring bean name — required non-blank and resolved at deploy time when providerType=BEAN.

providerVariable.description: Process variable name — required non-blank at deploy time when providerType=VARIABLE.

outgoing.description: Same shape as the common sequence flow, plus a gateway-specific constraint: at most one entry may set isDefault=true — DeployValidator rejects a gateway with more than one default edge (tier A). Zero default edges is legal (routing may rely purely on handlesNull/expectedAnswer matches).

parallelGateway.description: PARALLEL_GATEWAY — fans out to every outgoing edge unconditionally.

targetJoinId.description: Id of the JOIN_GATEWAY that closes this fork. NOT validated at deploy time — DeployValidator has no branch at all for PARALLEL_GATEWAY/JOIN_GATEWAY today; an unresolved or wrong-typed target only fails at runtime. There is also no minimum-outgoing-branches check — a PARALLEL_GATEWAY with 0 or 1 outgoing edges deploys fine, it just won't behave like a real fork.

joinGateway.description: JOIN_GATEWAY — waits for every branch spawned by the matching PARALLEL_GATEWAY, then continues via its own outgoing[0].

sourceSplitId.description: Id of the originating PARALLEL_GATEWAY. Purely informational — never read by the Navigator at runtime; the join's own outgoing[0] is what actually continues the flow after all branches complete.

boundaryInterruptiveTimer.description: BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER — a single-fire timer attached to a host node; firing interrupts the host.

attachedToRef.description: Id of the node this boundary timer is attached to.

executor.description: Present on this record but appears vestigial for timer nodes — not observed to be read anywhere in kikwi-core for this type.

providerType.description: NOT enforced at deploy time (tier B) — unlike EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY/correlation nodes, DeployValidator has no branch validating this node's own provider fields. A missing/mismatched provider only fails at runtime, inside TimerDueDateEvaluator.

staticValue.description: ISO-8601 duration (e.g. "PT1H") or an absolute ISO-8601 instant (e.g. "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z") — the evaluator tries Instant.parse first, then falls back to Duration.parse added to Instant.now().

boundaryNonInterruptiveTimer.description: BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER — a recurring timer attached to a host node; firing does NOT interrupt the host.

executor.description: Present on this record but appears vestigial — not observed to be read anywhere in kikwi-core for this type.

boundaryErrorHandler.description: BOUNDARY_ERROR_HANDLER — synchronous try/catch semantics on the host's thrown error code. The only boundary event type allowed on an EXECUTABLE_TASK.

errorCode.description: null means a wildcard/catch-all handler. The Navigator picks the first boundary handler — in the host's boundaryEventIds list order — whose errorCode is null or equals the thrown code; there is no explicit most-specific-first ordering.

boundaryInterruptiveCatchEvent.description: BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_CATCH_EVENT — waits for a correlated event; firing interrupts the host.

attachedToRef.description: Deploy-time enforced (tier A): must point to a node whose type is EXTERNAL_TASK or TIMER_TASK — no other host is accepted, not even EXECUTABLE_TASK or EVENT_CATCHER. This is one of the few boundaryEventIds/attachedToRef rules that IS a real deploy-blocking check today, even though this schema can't verify the referenced node's actual type (cross-node reference, outside JSON Schema's reach).

timerTask.description: TIMER_TASK — a main-flow (not boundary) single-fire timer. Not a WaitState, not Executable.

commitBefore.description: Whatever value is declared here is overridden at runtime — ProcessExecutionManager always treats a TIMER_TASK as commitBefore=true, since a timer can never execute synchronously. That override has no JSON-level signal; this field is accepted either way.

providerType.description: NOT enforced at deploy time (tier B) — DeployValidator has no branch validating this node's own provider fields. A missing/mismatched provider only fails at runtime, inside TimerDueDateEvaluator.

staticValue.description: ISO-8601 duration or absolute ISO-8601 instant — same parsing rule as BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER.staticValue.

boundaryEventIds.description: Deploy-time allowlist (tier A, referenced node types not checkable by this schema): BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER, BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER or BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_CATCH_EVENT. No BOUNDARY_ERROR_HANDLER — a TIMER_TASK has no synchronous handler to try/catch.

eventCatcher.description: EVENT_CATCHER — a wait state that resolves one or more correlation keys and waits for matching correlated events (STANDALONE = 1 key, GROUP = scatter-gather over N keys).

then.$comment: Deploy-time enforced (tier A): STATIC always resolves exactly one key, which makes no sense combined with GROUP's scatter-gather semantics.

boundaryEventIds.description: Deploy-time allowlist (tier A, referenced node types not checkable by this schema): only BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER or BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER node ids.

catchType.description: STANDALONE resolves exactly one key; GROUP is a scatter-gather over N keys (matchPolicy decides ALL vs ANY). GROUP combined with providerType=STATIC is rejected at deploy time.

eventThrower.description: EVENT_THROWER — a main-flow node (not a WaitState) that fires a correlated event and continues immediately. v1 policy is FAIL: if no catcher is currently waiting for the thrown key, the node fails and goes through the normal incident/retry path — it is never silently ignored.

callActivityCoordinator.description: CALL_ACTIVITY_COORDINATOR — starts one or more independent child ProcessInstances (a subprocess call). Simplified subprocess-only model: no bodyType/EMBEDDED, no branches list, no matchPolicy — each iteration is a full child process started via its own dedicated STARTER task.

boundaryEventIds.description: Deploy-time allowlist (tier A, referenced node types not checkable by this schema): only BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER or BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER node ids — no error handler, no catch event.

calledElement.description: Key of the process to call as a subprocess. Required non-blank at deploy time (tier A). NOT validated that a process with this key actually exists/is deployed.

collectionVariable.description: Process variable expected to resolve to a List at runtime — one child ProcessInstance is started per element (or a single implicit null element if this is omitted). Not validatable at deploy time; the engine has no variable-type system.

elementVariable.description: Only valid together with collectionVariable — deploy-time error (tier A) if set without it.

iterationMode.description: null is treated as PARALLEL at runtime. SEQUENTIAL starts only the first branch's child process and drips the rest as earlier children complete.
